posts.text: SCOTUS gives President Trump new powers. In a pair of decisions, the Supreme Court said that Donald Trump cannot fire Federal Reserve’s Lisa Cook without process and cause, but also recognized new and vast powers by the president to fire heads of agencies that, until today, were considered independent, and therefore, required justification before their removal.
posts.summary: Frames Supreme Court decision as granting Trump expansive new presidential powers

posts.text: What is the SAVE Act and can noncitizens vote U.S. federal elections today? Voting is a constitutional right ensured by several amendments to the Constitution, but laws that make it difficult for some U.S. citizens to vote make those rights harder to exercise.  Unlike @abdielwithtruth says, opposing the SAVE Act only means wanting to make sure all eligible citizens vote.
posts.summary: Defends voting rights against restrictive voter eligibility requirements

The Board of Education will vote on a mandatory reading list for public school students from first grade through 12th grade that includes several Bible passages, as required by Texas state law  The list includes only Bible passages and no other religions.
